summary: Round r1 (restricted network): primary sources located for audit irregularities and arrears (OAG annual reports and English executive summaries for the 52nd, 55th, 58th and the 62nd report), procurement practice (Public Procurement Act 2063 and Regulation 2064, PPMO annual reports, bolpatra e-GP, OCDS publication in the Open Contracting data registry, PEFA assessments incl. the 2022-cut-off national and a Gandaki subnational assessment), anti-corruption enforcement (CIAA annual reports) and perception indices (WGI 2025 with revised methodology; TI CPI 2025 dataset). No document could be downloaded and search-snippet figures were not used, so every quantitative item is pending. Key methodological constraints are already identifiable: WGI was revised in December 2025 (new 0-100 absolute scale, historical recalculation) so pre-2025 vintages must not be mixed with the new series; OAG coverage changed with federalisation, creating a break in irregularity and arrears series; CPI is comparable only from 2012.

findings.claim: Irregularities reported by the Auditor General by category (to be recovered, to be regularised, evidence not produced, advances) and tier, over successive annual reports
findings.note: OAG annual reports 52nd to 62nd (audit years FY2069/70 to FY2080/81): irregularity amounts by category and by federal/provincial/local tier, and as share of audited amount. Unit NPR_current_bn. Leads: old.oag.gov.np menu-category/926; executive summaries.

findings.claim: Cumulative outstanding irregularities and arrears (beruju) reported by the Auditor General
findings.note: Arrears table in each annual report: cumulative unsettled amount, settled during year, newly added. Note methodological breaks when the report added provincial and local tiers after federalisation.

findings.claim: Share of procurement value and contracts awarded via e-GP and via open competitive methods
findings.note: PPMO annual reports and OCDS data: value and count by procurement method; e-GP coverage by tier; user-committee and direct procurement shares. Leads: PPMO annual reports page; OCP registry publication 36.

findings.claim: Competition intensity: average bids per tender and single-bid share
findings.note: Computed from OCDS bid data (when retrievable) or PPMO report tables; state coverage (which entities publish).

findings.claim: WGI six dimensions for Nepal, 1996 onward, 2025 methodology
findings.note: Download WGI 2025 dataset: Nepal scores (0-100 absolute scale) with standard errors and number of sources; do not compare with pre-revision vintages' percentile ranks or -2.5..2.5 estimates without flagging the break.

findings.claim: CPI score and standard error for Nepal, 2012 onward
findings.note: CPI 2025 full dataset: scores 2012-2025 (comparable since 2012 methodology), standard error, number of sources. Calendar year of publication differs from underlying survey years.

findings.claim: CIAA complaints, cases filed and case outcomes
findings.note: CIAA annual reports (BS fiscal years): complaints received/settled, cases filed at Special Court, amounts claimed, conviction rate as reported by Special Court. Counts of cases need a unit code not present in units.py.

findings.claim: PEFA procurement and audit indicator scores 2015 vs 2022
findings.note: PEFA reports: PI-24, PI-26, PI-30, PI-31 letter scores; framework version differences between assessments to be noted.

data_gaps: OAG annual reports (Nepali full text and English summaries) 52nd-62nd: irregularity and arrears tables - download blocked.
PPMO annual reports: procurement by method and e-GP share - download blocked.
OCDS bulk data from Nepal e-GP (coverage period and completeness unknown) - download blocked.
CIAA annual reports - not located as direct PDF links; site access blocked.
WGI 2025 dataset and CPI 2025 dataset - download blocked.

assumptions.text: Perception indices (WGI, CPI) are recorded as perception measures of governance, not as measured corruption or procurement outcomes, and are not used as model drivers without a documented transmission channel.
OAG 'irregularity' (beruju) is an audit-observation category, not a measure of proven corruption; amounts to be regularised include documentation failures.
assumptions.basis_note: original label: 'assumption (definition to be confirmed from OAG report glossary)'

challenges.text: Any strategy claim citing a governance-index trend must specify WGI vintage; the December 2025 revision recalculated history and changed the scale, so older published figures are not comparable.
OAG irregularities by provincial and local tier should be linked to 11C's local capacity-gap evidence (LISA, FCNA) rather than treated separately.

uncertainty: High: no values retrieved in r1. Structural uncertainties: (i) OAG irregularity totals depend on audit coverage, which expanded after federalisation, so trends conflate coverage and behaviour; (ii) e-GP share may measure tender notices rather than contract value, and user-committee procurement lies largely outside e-GP; (iii) WGI and CPI are perception-based with wide standard errors, and WGI changed methodology in December 2025; (iv) Nepali fiscal years (mid-July) for OAG/PPMO/CIAA versus calendar years for WGI/CPI.

audit_irregularities_trend.method: Tabulate irregularities by category and tier and cumulative arrears from each OAG annual report (BS fiscal year of audit), flag the federalisation coverage break, express also as share of audited expenditure.

procurement_competition.method: Procurement value and count by method and channel (e-GP vs other) from PPMO annual reports; bids per tender and single-bid share from OCDS data; legal thresholds from PPA 2063/PPR 2064; PEFA PI-24 as qualitative cross-check.

governance_indicators.method: WGI 2025 (six dimensions, 0-100 absolute scale, with standard errors) and CPI 2012-2025 (with standard errors) for Nepal; methodology caveats: perception-based, overlapping underlying sources between WGI and CPI, WGI 2025 revision break, CPI calendar vs survey years.
